messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@cloudnexus.com>, Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@cloudnexus.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: Accelerated throughput roadmap & MAP for Dedicated GPU pool - CloudNexus

Hi Sarah / Ethan —

Great to meet you both last week. Per our call, I wanted to kick off a concise mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align on capacity, throughput targets, and a close timeline for the Dedicated GPU pool for CloudNexus. Below is a suggested starter plan and owners — please review and flag anything missing.

Summary objectives:
- Goal: Deliver a Dedicated GPU pool sized to sustain 2M tokens/day with 99th pct latency < 250ms for our primary LLM workloads (chat + reranking) by end of June.
- Initial evaluation window: 3 weeks of perf/cost telemetry with a canary fleet, followed by production ramp.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) Discovery (this week) — finalize workload profiles, peak QPS windows, and security requirements. Owner: CloudNexus (Sarah) + Redwood (Aditya).
2) Evaluation (1–3 weeks) — Redwood provides a dedicated canary pool, test harness, and sample throughput profile. Owner: Redwood (Karthik) + CloudNexus (Ethan).
3) Sizing & Pricing (week 2) — agree on pool size, burst policy, and reserved commit. Owner: Redwood Sales (Aditya) + Procurement (CloudNexus).
4) Contract & Security signoffs (week 3–4) — SOC2 evidence, network diagrams, and customer-run pen test window. Owner: Redwood Security + CloudNexus Security/Procurement.
5) Rollout & ramp (post-sign) — staged ramp to production with telemetry gating. Owner: Redwood Ops (Marissa) + CloudNexus Eng.

Attachments: I attached a starter MAP spreadsheet (MAP-CloudNexus-v1.xlsx) and a short throughput profile doc (throughput-profile.pdf). The sheet includes a column for absolute deadlines so we can convert this into milestones in HubSpot.

Immediate asks:
- Sarah: please confirm primary workload (chat vs. batch embeddings) and any hard latency SLAs beyond the 99th pct target above.
- Procurement: share preferred PO template & timeline constraints (cc'd procurement alias OK).
- Karthik/Marissa: can you scope the canary pool (GPU type + estimated nodes) so we have a sizing baseline by EOW?

Proposed 30-min sync to align owners and milestones: Tue Apr 20 at 10:00am PT — does that work for you?

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Accelerated throughput roadmap & MAP for Dedicated GPU pool - CloudNexus

Aditya — thanks, this looks great and very actionable. A few quick notes: 

- Primary workload: chat (multi-turn customer support) with periodic large-rank reranks for search. Peak QPS right now is small but expected to increase by ~4x during a product campaign in late May — we need headroom.
- Latency: our internal bar is 200ms median and 300ms 99th for chat; rerank can tolerate higher tail latency (up to 800ms).
- Procurement: I'll loop our procurement alias separately; we aim to have PO approvals in 2–3 weeks if pricing is confirmed.

I can make Tue Apr 20 10am PT. For the canary pool, Ethan can share a quick sample of the evaluation queries.

—Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Platform Engineering | CloudNexus

Aditya / team — quick engineering note after reviewing the throughput-profile.pdf and the initial MAP sheet:

- Canary suggestion: 4x A100s (or equivalent A2-family) for the first 72-hour test with a staged request profile (10%, 30%, 100%) to validate both latency SLOs and KV cache behavior. This should give telemetry to estimate steady-state nodes.
- KV cache: recommend we test both cold-start and warmed-KV scenarios; warmed KV reduces tokens per request by up to 25% for chat history use-cases.
- Autoscale/burst policy: propose a burst window (2x sustained) for marketing spikes — we should map costs for 2x vs 3x to show deployment tradeoffs.

I'll draft a short technical checklist for Tue's call and upload to the shared Drive. Marissa, Monica — can you own the ops runbook and success gates?

-Karthik
